Interface BeanResolutionTracer

public interface BeanResolutionTracer
Receives callbacks as the bean context creates beans and resolves their injection points, for example to log the resolution or to record it as spans of a trace.

A tracer is registered with ApplicationContextBuilder.beanResolutionTracer(BeanResolutionTracer), or created by a BeanResolutionTracerProvider discovered with ServiceLoader. Tracers exist before any bean does and therefore cannot be beans themselves. All active tracers, together with the tracer of the BeanResolutionTraceMode, receive every callback: the tracer of the mode first, then the registered tracers in the order they were registered, then the discovered tracers in the order of their providers. The class patterns of the BeanResolutionTraceConfiguration only restrict the tracer of the mode.

What is traced

The creation of every bean is traced, whether it is created to be resolved, for an injection point, or with one of the createBean methods of the BeanContext. The creation of a bean encloses the resolution of its injection points: the parameters of its constructor or factory method, its injected fields and methods, the beans named by its annotations and the events of its event listeners.

Threading and ordering

  • A callback is invoked on the thread that resolves the bean, synchronously. The callbacks of the creation of a bean and of the injection points it resolves, including the beans created for them, are all invoked on that thread. Separate beans may be created concurrently on separate threads, so a tracer must be thread safe.
  • Creations and injections nest strictly, like the frames of a call stack: every traceBeanCreation(Resolution, BeanDefinition, Argument) is followed, on the same thread, by exactly one traceBeanCreated(Resolution, BeanDefinition) or traceBeanCreationFailed(Resolution, BeanDefinition, Throwable), and every traceInjectBean(Resolution, Injection) by exactly one traceInjectComplete(Resolution, Injection) with the same BeanResolutionTracer.Injection, whether the injection succeeded or not. Any callback in between belongs to the innermost creation or injection still open. A tracer can therefore keep its open spans on a per thread stack.
  • A bean created to satisfy an injection point is reported between the traceInjectBean(Resolution, Injection) and the traceInjectComplete(Resolution, Injection) of that injection point. A bean that its creation looks up from the context programmatically is reported nested in it too, although it is part of another BeanResolutionTracer.Resolution.
  • When the creation of a bean fails, traceBeanCreationFailed(Resolution, BeanDefinition, Throwable) is invoked for it instead of traceBeanCreated(Resolution, BeanDefinition), after the open injection points of the bean were completed, and then again for each enclosing creation that the failure fails.

Callbacks run on the path that resolves every bean, so they should be fast. A tracer must not throw: an exception thrown by a callback propagates to, and fails, the resolution being traced, except one thrown by traceBeanCreationFailed(Resolution, BeanDefinition, Throwable), which is added as suppressed to the failure of the creation. Even then the pairing holds: the other tracers still receive the callback, and a creation or an injection whose start callback throws is ended at once with traceBeanCreationFailed(Resolution, BeanDefinition, Throwable) or traceInjectComplete(Resolution, Injection). A callback must not create beans either.

    • traceBeanCreation

      void traceBeanCreation(BeanResolutionTracer.Resolution resolution, BeanDefinition<?> beanDefinition, Argument<?> beanType)
      Start tracing the creation of a bean.

      The injection path is empty for a bean created on its own, and otherwise ends with the innermost injection point being resolved. That is the injection point the bean is created for, except for the factory of a bean produced by a factory: the lookup of the factory is not an injection point, so the path of the factory ends with the injection point the produced bean is created for, if any. The beans in creation do not include the bean yet.

      Parameters:
      resolution - The resolution in progress
      beanDefinition - The bean definition
      beanType - The bean type
